4.baseline: The initial Monster Truck build already had driving, suspension and procedural vehicle damage. The archive preserves its source and QC captures, followed by a seven-iteration refinement log and a final R7 build.

improvements.title: Contact geometry matches the visible car
improvements.description: Removed a uniform residual ride height and sampled local undeformed body height so the collision surface no longer hovered above the visible contact edge.

improvements.title: Camera and HUD become more readable
improvements.description: Added a wide wreckage view, corrected slow-motion framing and removed CSS ghosting during timeline jumps. The final composition keeps the truck and five damaged cars legible.

improvements.title: One coherent damage field
improvements.description: Side, end and roof surfaces now read the same damage field. Local creases, clearcoat and fill light make deformation visible instead of hidden between panels.

improvements.title: Physics and replay correctness
improvements.description: Damage is driven by actual ground travel and load. Attachments inherit local damage, debris receives approximate vehicle/tire collisions, and duplicate timeline events no longer contaminate deterministic replay.

improvements.title: Resource cleanup across resets
improvements.description: Replacement vehicles and debris explicitly release GPU resources. Geometry and texture counts remain stable in the final reset test instead of growing per cycle.

improvements.title: R7 tire contact and flattening
improvements.description: Support sampling increased from 5 to 21 points. Load-dependent tire flattening, sidewall bulging and deformed-geometry contact reports improved the final crush pose.

4.limitation: The simulation mixes vehicle dynamics, suspension support and procedural plastic deformation; it is not a full soft-body or node-beam solver. The recorded soak is about 30 seconds and does not prove long-term stability on every device. Not every intermediate source snapshot was retained.

comparisons.caption: The final pass improves ground contact, body alignment and the readability of the crush.
Shared damage fields and additional geometric refinement make roof deformation more coherent.

metrics: 21 support samples per tire (up from 5)
Geometry count stable at 499 and textures at 8 across the final 30.2-second reset soak
No browser errors in the final soak report

18.baseline: S.V. Kestrel preserves R0, R1 and R2 source snapshots. The Bottled Sea preserves a separate pre-refinement source archive and the current TypeScript implementation. These are related project lines, not one artificial four-release sequence.

improvements.title: R0 → R1: 50 documented details
improvements.description: The first refinement adds 50 enumerated visual and interaction details. Independent deterministic random streams preserve the original layout, while instancing and a centralized update function control the added animation cost.

improvements.title: R1 → R2: 50 more documented details
improvements.description: A second independent random stream and bake pass add weather-reactive jellyfish, rain rings, lightning reflections, cloud shadows and other scene behavior without resetting the earlier composition.

improvements.title: R4: glass, rigging and camera behavior
improvements.description: A later project line refines hollow glass, curve highlights, physical rigging and lighthouse beams. Manual camera selection now stops automatic rotation. Only the five actually documented R4 motion details are claimed.

improvements.title: Brighter studio and director timeline
improvements.description: The R4 presentation introduces a brighter studio, layered blue water and a wall-clock camera timeline so software rendering does not slow the intended transitions.

improvements.title: The Bottled Sea: source-level visual refinement
improvements.description: The preserved before/after sources show deeper water, richer storm mixing, wakes and spray, curved sails, physical rigging, ship lights, adjusted glass reflections and rebalanced day/night fill and rim lighting.

improvements.title: Non-destructive recording and deterministic fallback
improvements.description: Output and frame paths can be redirected instead of overwriting earlier takes. A wider final hero shot and explicit fallback state improve repeatable recording.

18.limitation: R4 is a separate refinement line, not a continuous R2→R4 snapshot chain. Water uses wave functions, spring damping and sampling approximations rather than a full fluid solver. The archive records successful build, interaction and playback checks; the complete verify:record regression was not rerun during packaging.
metrics: R1: 50 enumerated additions
R2: 50 further additions
9 build and interaction checks passed, including 390px touch layout
Dual-video playback passed with zero browser errors

23.baseline: The earliest retained Fjord scene is a single-file Three.js seaplane study with mountains, forest, village, waterfalls and a 22-second flight path. It already contains first-pass water and exposure work, so the original one-shot is not claimed.

improvements.title: Water and exposure
improvements.description: A fourth high-frequency ripple layer, sky reflection and glints were added. Exposure increased from 1.28 to 1.35 and hemisphere light from 0.95 to 1.05, with brighter distant haze.

improvements.title: Terrain and reflected color
improvements.description: Turquoise water, mountain-streak reflections, dual glints and wave shadows were paired with ice fissures, stronger displacement, green slopes and clearer cliff contrast.

improvements.title: Float contact and camera arc
improvements.description: Aircraft waypoints rose four meters to correct submerged floats. The camera was reorganized into aerial establishment, water-level approach, close flyby and panoramic pull-back.

improvements.title: Reflections and secondary motion
improvements.description: Planar reflection, wind patches, waterfall-foot rings, foam and subtle camera sway connected the terrain, aircraft and water.

improvements.title: Composition and scale
improvements.description: The middle shot moved from roughly 24m to 40–46m, then pulled back about 1.35× with a higher angle. Aircraft scale changed from 1.3 to 1.05 to reduce clipping and preserve the mountain frame.

improvements.title: Wake physics and frame-step bug
improvements.description: A V-wake, takeoff burst, expanding foam and denser spray were added. Frame capture changed from tick(0) to a fixed 1/30 step so particle lifetimes actually advanced.

improvements.title: Two-stage clipping repair
improvements.description: Cliff-edge vertices first received height variation; the problematic independent cliff pieces were then removed. Waterfalls now follow the same mountain displacement and trees use the makePeak height function while avoiding waterfall channels.

improvements.title: Final implementation and edit rhythm
improvements.description: The final entry switched to a separate 25-second alpine-lake implementation. Its edit compresses the first 15 seconds to 3, expands the remaining 10 to 16, and holds the final frame for 3 seconds.

23.limitation: The original one-shot and every intermediate source snapshot were not retained. Most sequence details come from the technical process log. The final alpine-lake entry is a different implementation and must not be credited with every earlier scene modification.

comparisons.caption: The final archive capture documents the implementation switch and the cleaner, more open composition.

metrics: 22-second final comparison timeline
Fixed 1/30-second frame capture step
Final aircraft visible from the third second in the edited sequence

24.baseline: The retained one-shot already had custom whale cross-sections, long pectoral fins, flukes, throat pleats, procedural ocean, broken water crowns and gravity droplets. Later work split into a Blender asset branch and an 11-second lateral Three.js branch.

improvements.title: Breach orientation
improvements.description: Pitch, yaw and roll keys were refined so the whale reads as a lateral breach rather than a rigid vertical pose.

improvements.title: Blender ocean and distant water
improvements.description: Regular wave stripes were replaced by multi-scale geometric waves and stretched noise. A distant-ocean ring and matched materials reduced visible tiling and the far-water seam.

improvements.title: Procedural spray and foam
improvements.description: Broken thin sheets, expanding foam rings and 2,450 Geometry Nodes emission points created gravity-driven droplets with irregular edges.

improvements.title: Verified asset orientation
improvements.description: The existing procedural whale was imported into Blender as 66 meshes and 17,992 triangles. Native −Y and side views were rendered before applying Z=-90°, avoiding guessed orientation.

improvements.title: Material and water-entry corrections
improvements.description: Micro-noise bump, revised roughness and coating improved the skin. A rectangular deep-water volume caused a dark band and was disabled while preserving geometric waves and IOR. All 244 affected water-entry frames were rerendered.

improvements.title: An 11-second lateral choreography
improvements.description: The Three.js branch uses a fixed low camera and an 11-second action rather than a simple speed-up. The whale travels 23.4m, about 1.857 body lengths, with head contact at 5.667 seconds.

improvements.title: Surface, anatomy and spray finishing
improvements.description: Five Gerstner-style wave groups, 19 geometric throat pleats, asymmetric swept fins, low sun, islands and birds were combined with separated droplets, mist, broken sheets and uneven foam.

24.limitation: The five self-refinement rounds do not have individual source snapshots. Blender asset work and the lateral Three.js version are parallel branches, not one linear stack. The archive presents the lateral branch as its final browser scene and keeps the Blender evidence separate.

comparisons.caption: The lateral branch replaces the narrow vertical read with a clearer body silhouette, longer travel and calmer ocean composition.
The Blender branch continues pitch beyond vertical and lowers the body for a more convincing entry.

metrics: Lateral source: 660 frames at 60fps, 11 seconds
Blender branch: 528 rendered frames at 24fps, 22 seconds
244 water-entry frames rerendered
23.4m lateral travel; apex at 4.5s

25.baseline: The starting point was an existing Blender asset: 49,714 vertices, 14 bones, 65 frames at 24fps, a 50mm camera and original animation. This project refined that asset; it did not remodel the deer or claim a new gait.

improvements.title: Asset integrity and portability
improvements.description: The original mesh, rig and action were preserved without retopology. Three external textures were packed into the final Blender file and verified after reopening.

improvements.title: Orientation and camera alignment
improvements.description: Whole-model yaw and pitch were aligned to zero while retaining the 50mm lens and original camera translation.

improvements.title: Systematic light search
improvements.description: Thirty key-light directions and five sun angles were evaluated on frame 13. The selected (0.35, 0.4, -0.8) direction and 0.12rad sun angle brought shadow direction and length closer to the reference.

improvements.title: Short-fur material refinement
improvements.description: Scale-220 fine noise, Bump strength 0.12 at distance 0.002, Sheen 0.06 and Specular 0.45 created a restrained short-fur surface without a plastic highlight.

improvements.title: Occlusion, shadows and anti-aliasing
improvements.description: GTAO was enabled at distance 0.35 and quality 1.0. EEVEE samples increased from 64 to 256, shadow rays from 1 to 4 and shadow steps from 6 to 8.

improvements.title: Honest motion presentation
improvements.description: The original 16-frame gait and camera motion were retained. Because the direct loop seam was visible, the deliverables became a 65-frame source-length cut and a 16-second motion-compensated slow-motion cut instead of a claimed seamless loop.

25.limitation: The 0–1 pixel result refers only to bounding-box edges on five representative frames, not complete visual equivalence. The 16-second cut uses bidirectional motion-compensated interpolation, not 384 newly rendered frames or a newly authored 16-second gait. The public reference is not a controlled regeneration comparison.

comparisons.caption: Orientation, light direction, short-fur shading and shadow settings were refined while preserving the original asset and animation.

metrics: Bounding-box edges differ by 0–1px on five checked frames
49,714 vertices and 14 bones preserved
65 source frames at 24fps; 384-frame interpolated slow-motion cut
256 EEVEE samples, 4 shadow rays, 8 shadow steps
